context:
Start with evidence, not edits: build a full clone-group matrix before changing code.
For each group classified as parallel_implementation, identify the narrowest shared abstraction
point (utility function, mixin, or core helper module) and migrate incrementally.
Keep each consolidation track independently testable and committable.
Apply ignore rules only after explicit group-level classification and only with narrow scope.
Re-run duplicate scan after each consolidation track to confirm the expected impact.
description:
The latest `make duplicate-check-verbose` run reports 401 duplicate function groups and
13,796 duplicated lines (threshold 15,180). The first consolidation pass removed high-value
duplicates, but the report still contains many mixed groups where some are intentional
boilerplate while others are true parallel implementations.

This follow-up TODO performs a full classification pass for all currently identified clone
groups, then applies the correct action for each class:
- Intended duplication: keep implementation but mark with narrow ignore rules.
- Parallel implementation: centralize shared logic into core modules/mixins/helpers and update call sites.

The key deliverable is a complete, auditable triage map of every reported clone group plus
implementation work that lowers duplicated lines further and reduces noise in future reports.

anti_patterns.dont: change public benchmark facade signatures during refactor
anti_patterns.why: downstream modules and tests rely on them

anti_patterns.dont: consolidate structurally similar but domain-specific SQL/generator logic
ignore whole directories in duplicate config
anti_patterns.instead: use narrow function/path-level ignores tied to classified groups.

anti_patterns.dont: introduce deep inheritance chains for consolidation

preserves.behavior: DataFrame adapter correctness for pandas-family and expression-family query execution paths.
Duplicate checker remains useful (no broad ignores that hide real regressions).
Firebolt/Presto/Trino execution semantics and error handling behavior in platform adapter tests.
Spark-family load paths continue to support current file formats and loading options.
Top-level benchmark facade APIs (`get_query`, `get_queries`, `get_create_tables_sql`) remain backwards compatible.

verifications.command: uv run -- python -c "import json,yaml,pathlib; r=pathlib.Path('_project/quality/duplicate-code-followup/latest-duplicates.json'); m=pathlib.Path('_project/quality/duplicate-code-followup/classification-matrix.yaml'); report=json.loads(r.read_text()); matrix=yaml.safe_load(m.read_text()); rows=matrix['groups'] if isinstance(matrix,dict) and 'groups' in matrix else matrix; report_ids={g['hash'] for g in report['groups']}; matrix_ids={row['group_hash'] for row in rows}; missing=report_ids-matrix_ids; extra=matrix_ids-report_ids; assert not missing and not extra, f'missing={len(missing)} extra={len(extra)}'; print(f'coverage_ok groups={len(report_ids)}')"
verifications.description: All clone groups in current report have explicit classifications and actions
verifications.expected: coverage_ok groups=<count>, with zero missing/extra group hashes.

verifications.description: Core duplicate checker passes at new threshold
verifications.expected: PASS with duplicated lines below updated threshold.

verifications.description: Targeted platform and dataframe tests remain green after consolidation
